chapter_title: The Chapter of the Name of the Fathers

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
The Divine as first made present and fixed for reception is acknowledged as the originating Love in unmeasured power. That power is the whole ultimate plane in which this Love abides as stable being; within it, wisdom in its pure essence shines forth and encompasses every abundance of heavenly goods and truths, together with all angelic states and all ordered communities of reception, and the outermost determination of that wisdom’s shining is set as what governs the whole.

Also, the mediating Divine that proceeds as a third in the order of manifestation is likewise acknowledged as an originating source. Its unmeasured power is the active conveyance in which love is alive within wisdom and wisdom is alive within love, and within that living union it dwells as what is fixed for use.

Again, the Divine Human made manifest as saving wisdom is likewise acknowledged as an originating source. Its unmeasured power is the living conveyance of truth as it proceeds from love into lower degrees for restoration, and within that living truth it dwells as what is established.

paragraph_translations.translation: The Divine as first made present and fixed for reception is to be acknowledged as the originating Love in unmeasured power. That unmeasured power is the whole ultimate plane in which this Love abides as stable being, and within that same plane its inmost being of wisdom shines forth and encompasses every abundance of heavenly goods and truths, together with all angelic states and all ordered communities of reception; and the outermost determination of that shining wisdom is set as what governs the whole.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the naming of the first principle by unfolding what its “greatness” is as an ultimate plane held under the rule of wisdom’s boundary.
paragraph_translations.notes: The phrase about “root” repeats establishment in the ultimate plane; I absorbed it into the stability of Love’s presence.

paragraph_translations.translation: Further, the mediating Divine that proceeds as a third in the order of manifestation is also to be acknowledged as an originating source. Its unmeasured power is the living conveyance in which love and wisdom act as one in outward operation, and within that active union it dwells as what is fixed for use.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by extending the title of originating source to a third-order proceeding Divine and defining its operative greatness.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Third Ambassador” has no function beyond being the third proceeding mediator; I translated by that role.

paragraph_translations.translation: Again, the Divine Human made manifest as saving wisdom is likewise to be acknowledged as an originating source. Its unmeasured power is living truth proceeding from love in active conveyance, within which it dwells and by which it is established.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by applying the same pattern to saving wisdom in the form nearest to reception, shifting emphasis to truth’s restorative life.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Jesus the Splendour” functions here as saving wisdom; I translated by that function.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Highly coherent: each paragraph repeats a single doctrinal pattern—an originating Divine is named as “father,” then its “greatness” is described as the stable plane or living conveyance in which it dwells and is established. The voice is consistent; differences are purposeful shifts of degree: ultimate stability, mediating active union, then living truth for restoration.

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: the teaching proceeds by function (what “greatness/earth/light” does) and builds an organic cosmology (plane → indwelling → encompassing → boundary) without administrative listing.
findings.evidence: Text teaches by functional relations: “His greatness is the great earth where he lives, he being established in it… the essence of the light that swathes… and the boundary of the light is set over it.” The spiritual reading reports no narrative stumble here and explicitly notes only a minor repetition (“The phrase about ‘root’ repeats establishment… I absorbed it…”), which is typical of restored/damaged duplication rather than a voice switch. Nothing is organized by jurisdiction, rank, or named offices; instead, the correspondential sense arises from the described operations: ‘earth’ as established plane, ‘light’ as encompassing, ‘boundary’ as outer determination.

findings.diagnosis: Insertion of administrative titulature into an otherwise functional pattern: “Third Ambassador” is an office-name from Mani’s administrative cosmology, and it interrupts the otherwise purely descriptive ‘Father → greatness as vessel/plane’ formula by introducing governance-style identification (a rank/role label) rather than a functional natural basis.
findings.evidence: The pattern matches ¶3: “they shall call X ‘father’. His greatness is Y… wherein he lives, he being established in it.” However, the X in ¶4 is not a functional/natural term but an administrative title: “the Third Ambassador.” The spiritual reading itself signals a stumble: “Third Ambassador has no function beyond being the third proceeding mediator; I translated by that role.” That is exactly the diagnostic: the reader cannot derive meaning from what it *does* inside this sentence, only from the fact that it is “third” (ordering/rank) and “ambassador” (office). The rest of the sentence (“light ship of living fire”) returns to correspondential imagery, suggesting an overlayed name inserted into a functional template.
findings.scope: Furthermore, they shall call the Third Ambassador ‘father’.

findings.diagnosis: Expansion at a seam via christological identification: the historical/theological proper name “Jesus the Splendour” is a Mani-layer identification that recasts a functional figure into a named authority. It fits the template syntactically, but it shifts the teaching from correspondential function to institutional/theological labeling.
findings.evidence: Like ¶4, the sentence is template-driven: “Once again, X… shall… be called ‘father’. His greatness is the ship of living waters…” The correspondential substance is in the ‘ship’ and ‘living waters’ imagery (function/vessel), but the insertion is the proper-name identification “Jesus the Splendour.” The spiritual reading again notes compensatory translation: “Jesus the Splendour functions here as saving wisdom; I translated by that function.” That admission indicates the name is not participating organically in the functional exposition but is being reinterpreted to preserve coherence—typical of Mani’s seam-additions that identify an eternal function with a named figure.
findings.scope: Once again, Jesus the Splendour shall himself also be called ‘father’.

textual_criticism.summary: 3 findings total: 1 clean correspondential substrate confirmation (¶3, no action). 2 disruptions where the spiritual reading had to translate names by role/function (¶4–¶5): both are mixed-voice seams where administrative/christological identifiers are inserted into an otherwise functional ‘father/greatness/vessel’ template. Recommended excisions: the naming clauses in ¶4 and ¶5; the remaining ‘greatness is the ship…’ lines preserve a smoother correspondential narrative.

harmonized_paragraphs.text: Now, the Father, who is the first established thing, shall be called ‘the Father of Greatness’. His greatness is the great earth where he lives, he being established in it [as the great earth, and his root is in it; and] the essence of the light that swathes all the rich gods and the angels and the dwellings [of this greatness; and the boundary of the light] is set over it.
His greatness is the light ship of living fire wherein he lives, he being established in it.
His greatness is the ship of living waters where he lives, he being established in it.

changes_summary: ¶4: Excised the naming clause “Furthermore, they shall call the Third Ambassador ‘father’.” per Finding 2 (administrative titulature interrupting the functional template). ¶5: Excised the naming clause “Once again, Jesus the Splendour shall himself also be called ‘father’.” per Finding 3 (proper-name christological identification as a seam expansion). ¶3 unchanged per Finding 1 (recommendation: none).
